title: Pump rates that need rounding to the nearest whole number
blurb: Round pump rates correctly: half-up, at the very end, to exactly the places the stem asks for.
question: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 1000 mL, IV, over 14 hours, start 0800. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

teach.body: Formal rule: work with the full calculator value and round only the final answer, half-up, to the precision the stem asks for. Plain English: if the digit after the last one you keep is 5 or more, round up; if it is 4 or less, leave it. On a Pearson practice paper, 1000 mL over 6 hours (166.67) was marked correct as 167.
teach.cite: Pearson VUE NMC practice test (adult Paper 1); answer-format guidance

teach.h: Worked example: Mrs Patel on a surgical ward
teach.body: Meera Patel, 58, has a chart row: 0.9% sodium chloride 1000 mL over 14 hours, start 0800, nearest whole number. 1000 ÷ 14 = 71.43. The first decimal is 4, so round down: 71 mL per hour. Sense-check: 71 × 14 = 994 mL, close to 1000 mL. Type 71.

teach.caption: Rounding the hours early changes the final answer.

teach.text: Rounding too early. Turning 40 minutes into 0.67 or 0.7 hours before dividing gives 149 or 143 instead of 150. Keep fractions exact (multiply by 60 and divide by the minutes) and round only the last answer.

teach.body: Pearson marks the format as well as the number. For a whole number, type 167, not 167.0. For one decimal place, type 166.7, not 167 or 166.67. Never add a trailing zero. If you only remember one rule: one rounding, at the end, to the instruction in the stem.
teach.cite: Pearson VUE NMC practice tests, answer-format guidance

items.label: rounding step, at the very end

items: Round only the final answer, never the hours or an intermediate step.
Half-up: 5 or more rounds up; 4 or less rounds down.
Nearest whole number means no decimal point in the answer.
Truncating (cutting off digits) is not rounding.
Type exactly the places asked, with no trailing zero.

summary: You can now round pump rates correctly to the nearest whole number or one decimal place, using half-up rounding on the final answer only. You can also see why rounding minutes to hours early gives the wrong rate.

A.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 1000 mL, IV, over 14 hours, start 0800. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
A.why: 1000 ÷ 14 = 71.43. The first decimal is 4, so round down: 71 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This rounds up; 71.43 rounds down because the first decimal is 4.
whyNot.2: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.
whyNot.3: This adds a zero to the volume, a tenfold error.

A.q: Prescription: 5% glucose, 500 mL, IV, over 3 hours, start 1000. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
A.why: 500 ÷ 3 = 166.67. The first decimal is 6, so round up: 167 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This cuts off the decimals instead of rounding 166.67 up.
whyNot.1: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.
whyNot.2: This rounds to the nearest ten, not the nearest whole number.

A.q: Prescription: an antibiotic in 0.9% sodium chloride, 100 mL, IV, over 40 minutes, start 1400. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
A.why: 100 × 60 ÷ 40 = 150 mL per hour exactly. No rounding is needed if you keep the minutes exact.

whyNot.1: This rounds 40 minutes to 0.67 hours too early, giving 149.
whyNot.2: This rounds 40 minutes to 0.7 hours too early, giving 143.
whyNot.3: This divides by the minutes, not the hours (2.5 rounds to 3).

B.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 250 mL, IV, over 7 hours, start 0600. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
B.why: 250 ÷ 7 = 35.71. The first decimal is 7, so round up: 36 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This cuts off the decimals instead of rounding 35.71 up.
whyNot.1: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.
whyNot.3: This multiplies volume by time instead of dividing.

B.q: Prescription: 0.18% sodium chloride with 4% glucose, 2200 mL, IV, over 24 hours, start 0800. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
B.why: 2200 ÷ 24 = 91.67. The first decimal is 6, so round up: 92 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This cuts off the decimals instead of rounding 91.67 up.
whyNot.2: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.

B.q: Prescription: an antibiotic in 0.9% sodium chloride, 100 mL, IV, over 35 minutes, start 1800. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
B.why: 100 × 60 ÷ 35 = 171.43. The first decimal is 4, so round down: 171 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This rounds 35 minutes to 0.58 hours too early, giving 172.
whyNot.1: This rounds 35 minutes to 0.6 hours too early, giving 167.
whyNot.2: This divides by the minutes, not the hours (2.86 rounds to 3).

C.q: A man is prescribed 1 unit of red cells, volume 350 mL, IV over 3 hours, start 1400. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
C.why: 350 ÷ 3 = 116.67. The first decimal is 6, so round up: 117 mL per hour.

whyNot.1: This cuts off the decimals instead of rounding 116.67 up.
whyNot.2: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.

C.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 1000 mL, IV, over 13 hours. The pump can be set to one decimal place. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Write your answer to one decimal place.
C.why: 1000 ÷ 13 = 76.923. The second decimal is 2, so 76.9 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This gives a whole number; the stem asks for one decimal place.
whyNot.1: This gives two decimal places; the stem asks for one.
whyNot.3: This adds a zero to the volume, a tenfold error.

C.q: A 1000 mL bag of 0.9% sodium chloride has 650 mL left in it. The prescriber asks for the remaining volume to run over the next 7 hours. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
C.why: 650 ÷ 7 = 92.86. The first decimal is 8, so round up: 93 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This cuts off the decimals instead of rounding 92.86 up.
whyNot.2: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.
whyNot.3: This uses the full 1000 mL, not the 650 mL remaining.

reteach.title: Look one digit to the right
reteach.question: A pump rate works out at 91.67. What do you type for the nearest whole number?

blocks.body: The digit after the units is 6, which is 5 or more, so add one: 92. If it had been 91.43, the 4 means you keep 91.

blocks.text: Cutting off the decimals (91.67 → 91) is truncating, not rounding.

explain.body: A 5 in the first decimal place rounds up. 83.5 becomes 84.

test.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 167 mL, IV, over 2 hours. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
test.why: 167 ÷ 2 = 83.5. A 5 rounds up: 84 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This rounds the 5 down; half-up rounding takes 83.5 to 84.
whyNot.1: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.
whyNot.2: This multiplies volume by time instead of dividing.

test.q: Prescription: an antibiotic in 0.9% sodium chloride, 50 mL, IV, over 20 minutes. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.

whyNot.1: This rounds 20 minutes to 0.33 hours too early, giving 152.
whyNot.2: This rounds 20 minutes to 0.3 hours too early, giving 167.
whyNot.3: This divides by the minutes, not the hours.

explain.h: Round down when the next digit is small

test.q: Prescription: 5% glucose, 750 mL, IV, over 9 hours. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Give your answer to the nearest whole number.
test.why: 750 ÷ 9 = 83.33. The first decimal is 3, so round down: 83 mL per hour.

whyNot.1: This gives one decimal place; the stem asks for a whole number.
whyNot.3: This multiplies volume by time instead of dividing.

test.q: Prescription: 0.9% sodium chloride, 500 mL, IV, over 3 hours. The pump can be set to one decimal place. At what rate should the infusion pump be set, in mL per hour? Write your answer to one decimal place.
test.why: 500 ÷ 3 = 166.666…. The second decimal is 6, so round up: 166.7 mL per hour.

whyNot.0: This gives a whole number; the stem asks for one decimal place.
whyNot.2: This cuts off the decimals instead of rounding up.
whyNot.3: This gives two decimal places; the stem asks for one.
